clips.title: Calling All Mutants: Getting Started with Mutation Testing
clips.why: A clear, short explanation of why passing tests and high coverage can still miss bugs, and how planting changes in the code shows it.
look: The problem with coverage: a line can run in a test without anything checking its result.
A mutant is a small planted change; a test suite should kill it by failing.
A mutant that survives points at a test that cannot fail for that change.
clips.after: verify asks for one hand-planted bug per new check; a mutation tool is the same idea run hundreds of times.

clips.title: TDD Reward Hacking: Why Your Coding Agent is Cheating
clips.why: Coding agents write weak assertions too, and this part shows how mutation testing catches tests that pass whatever the code does.
look: Weak assertions and incomplete mock checks: tests that look complete but accept wrong results.
Mutation testing as the way to catch them, instead of reading every test by hand.
clips.after: That is why Nova's checks must fail on an assertion before the change and why verify plants a bug after it: an agent's green test is a claim until it has failed once.

practice.q: Make the C1 test compare the exact message, so a wrong message fails.
practice.hint: The assertion that compares two values, not one that checks a value exists.
practice.why: assert.ok passes for any non-empty message. Comparing with the exact text is what lets a planted bug fail the test.

practice.q: Put the planted-bug habit in order.
items: Run the new check on your change and see it pass
Change one condition or value inside the behaviour the check is about
Run the check and read why it failed: expected against actual
Revert the planted change and see the check pass again
Write one line in the pull request about what you planted
practice.why: Pass, break, fail for the right reason, restore, record. The record is what the reviewer sees.

practice.q: C3 says that 1,000 projects show 25 rows on the first page. Which planted bug tests C3 best?

options.why: It breaks exactly the behaviour C3 is about, and a good C3 test fails with expected 25, actual 50.
Every test would crash on the import. That says nothing about C3.
That tests C2. Each check needs a planted bug in its own behaviour.

practice.q: A test suite has 100% line coverage of tableView. Can it still miss the wrong-message bug?

options.why: Every line ran. Whether any assertion checked the result is a different question.

options.text: Yes, if the assertions are weak, such as assert.ok on the message
options.why: Coverage counts lines that ran; only a failing assertion on a planted bug shows the test would notice.

options.text: Only if the tests run in parallel
options.why: Running order has nothing to do with it. The assertion does.
